steps: Create a button in HTML and give it an id so JavaScript can identify it.
Use JavaScript to select the button and add a click event listener.
Inside the event function, change the page background color using `document.body.style.backgroundColor`.
When the user clicks the button, the click event calls `changeBackgroundColor()`.
The function changes the `backgroundColor` style of the document’s body to light blue.
items.finalAnswer: A button click runs a JavaScript function that changes the page background color.

steps: CSS animations and transitions are used to change the appearance of an element gradually.
A transition smoothly changes a CSS property from one value to another when an event occurs, such as moving the mouse over an element.
The `transition` property specifies the CSS property to change, the duration, and optionally the timing function and delay.
In this example, the button’s background color changes smoothly from blue to green over one second when the pointer is placed over it.
A CSS animation can change an element’s style through a sequence of steps defined by `@keyframes`.
The `animation` property sets the animation name, duration, timing function, delay, number of repetitions, and direction as needed.
Here, `@keyframes` defines the movement, `moveBox` is the animation name, `2s` is its duration, and `infinite` repeats it continuously.
Transitions are generally triggered by a change in state, while animations can run automatically and can have several keyframe steps.
items.finalAnswer: Transitions smoothly change CSS properties between states; animations use `@keyframes` to apply changes over time.
